newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise, foreign buying seen.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise, foreign buying seen.

text.p: Argentine bonds opened higher Monday as traders noted that there were some flows, notably from abroad, coming back into the market.

"We saw some important purchases this morning from abroad," said a trader at an Argentine bank. A stronger Mexican peso and data released after the close of the market Friday showing strong tax receipts helped the market rise.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/2 to 83-1/2, while the local dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.30 to 119.65.
The Economy Ministry said Friday tax revenue in October was $3.72 billion, 12.5 percent higher than the same month a year earlier and 12.9 percent up on September.
"I am more optimistic, the situation for bonds is favorable," said Hugo Diaz Lourenco, senior analyst at financial consultancy C&E Consultores.
The market started recovering at the end of last week, aided by strong U.S. Treasuries on the back of U.S. economic indicators pointing to moderating economic growth.
And that recovery was seen being helped by local factors this week, mainly in the form of economic indicators that should lend more evidence of a rebound in growth.
